title: The surveyor's chain
place: Fields of the Herbert of White Friars estate, Llandough-juxta-Penarth

cast.E_AGENT: the estate surveyor (Herbert of White Friars / Hurst estate), unnamed

shots.direction: About 9 s. Date-and-place card over a wide establishing still on an early autumn morning around 1786. The camera stands on the inland crest of Llandough hill and looks down over hedged fields, Leckwith woods, the River Ely winding through the marshes, and the estuary far off in a pale haze. Two small figures and a plane-table stand in the middle distance. A slow push-in. Ambience: wind, rooks, a distant cowbell.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 landscape, Vale of Glamorgan c. 1786, early autumn morning. The view runs from an inland hilltop down over small hedged fields and earth banks, oak woods to one side, and a winding river through flat green-brown marshland, with a distant estuary in soft haze. The hill is not on the coast. Two tiny figures in 18th-century dress stand in a field beside a wooden plane-table on a tripod, with a thin measuring chain on the grass. Overcast silver light, muted greens and browns. No text, no heraldry, no buildings in the foreground.

captions.text: c. 1786 · Fields of the Herbert of White Friars estate, Llandough-juxta-Penarth

shots.direction: About 10 s. A low angle along the grass. A Gunter's chain lies taut between two iron arrows, and its brass tallies catch the light. Dai's boots plant a ranging pole at the hedge-bank. The camera tracks slowly along the chain. Ambience: chain links clinking, wind in the hedge. Caption only, no voice.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 close low-angle shot in a Welsh field c. 1786. An iron surveyor's Gunter's chain is stretched taut across rough grass between iron marking arrows, with small brass tally tags on the links. A big man's worn leather buckled shoes and woollen stockings stand at the far end beside a red-and-white wooden ranging pole planted at a hawthorn hedge-bank. Overcast light, shallow depth of field. Period-accurate. No text, no heraldry.

captions.text: Estate plans of lands in Cogan, Llandough, Penarth, St Andrews Major and Sully, 1786–1832, survive in the Percy Randell collection (CH-0004). This survey day is recreated as the most likely moment.

shots.direction: About 7 s. Medium shot of the surveyor at his plane-table, pencil in hand. He looks down the field and calls to Dai, who is off-frame at the far end of the chain.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium shot, Welsh hillside field c. 1786. A pale, clean-shaven man in his 50s wears thin-rimmed round spectacles, a dark wool frock coat, a waistcoat, breeches and a black round hat. He stands at a wooden plane-table on a tripod with a brass sighting rule and a sheet of paper pinned down, and a leather document case hangs at his side. He is calling across the field. Overcast light, hedgerows behind him. Invented face. No text, no heraldry.

lines.cy: Dai, tyn y gadwyn yn dynn. Cant o ddolenni, dim un yn llai.
lines.en: Dai, pull the chain tight. A hundred links, not one fewer.
lines.es: Dai, tensá bien la cadena. Cien eslabones, ni uno menos.
lines.review: cy: native review (mutations: yn dynn, o ddolenni)

shots.direction: About 9 s. Medium shot of Dai at the hedge-bank, ranging pole in one fist and the chain end in the other. He counts with his eyes back along the chain, then grins across the field at the surveyor.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium shot, c. 1786. A big bald Welshman in his 60s with ginger-grey mutton-chop whiskers wears a coarse linen shirt with rolled sleeves, a brown wool waistcoat, breeches and woollen stockings. He holds a red-and-white wooden ranging pole and the brass handle of an iron surveyor's chain beside a hawthorn hedge-bank and a wooden stile. He has a good-humoured, weathered face and is speaking across the field. Overcast light. Invented face. No text, no heraldry.

lines.cy: Dyna hi, syr. Pedair cadwyn o'r clawdd i'r gamfa. Ond pam mesur bryn sy wedi bod 'ma erioed?
lines.en: There she is, sir. Four chains from the hedge to the stile. But why measure a hill that's always been here?
lines.es: Ahí está, señor. Cuatro cadenas del cerco al paso. ¿Pero para qué medir una loma que estuvo acá desde siempre?
lines.review: cy: native review (i'r gamfa, sy wedi, 'ma)

shots.direction: About 9 s. Close on the surveyor. He lifts his eyes from the pinned sheet and gestures with the pencil across the wide view, naming the parishes one by one.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 close-medium shot, c. 1786. A pale, clean-shaven estate surveyor in his 50s with thin-rimmed spectacles, a dark frock coat and a round hat gestures with a pencil toward a wide valley of hedged fields and distant marshes. A plane-table with a pinned paper sheet and a brass sighting rule stands before him. He is speaking calmly. Overcast inland hilltop light. Invented face. No text, no heraldry.

lines.cy: Achos mae'r ystad moyn gweld ar bapur beth sy 'da hi. Cogan, Llandochau, Penarth, Sain Andras, Sili. Pob cae, pob clawdd.
lines.en: Because the estate wants to see on paper what it holds. Cogan, Llandough, Penarth, St Andrews, Sully. Every field, every hedge.
lines.es: Porque la finca quiere ver en papel lo que tiene. Cogan, Llandough, Penarth, St Andrews, Sully. Cada campo, cada cerco.
lines.review: cy: native review (moyn, sy 'da hi: southern forms; Sain Andras for St Andrews Major)

shots.direction: About 7 s. Dai turns and looks downhill toward the river and marshes. Over his shoulder, the Ely glints far below. He nods toward it and speaks.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 over-the-shoulder shot, c. 1786. A big bald man with ginger-grey mutton-chops and a brown waistcoat looks down from an inland hillside over hedged fields to a winding river and broad marshland, with a hazy estuary very far off. He holds a ranging pole and turns his head slightly to speak. Overcast light. Invented face. No text, no heraldry, no coastline in the foreground.

lines.cy: A'r afon? Elái a'r morfa lawr fan 'na. Chi'n mesur rheiny 'fyd?
lines.en: And the river? The Ely and the marsh down there. Are you measuring those too?
lines.es: ¿Y el río? El Ely y el bañado allá abajo. ¿También los va a medir?

shots.direction: About 8 s. The surveyor bends to the sighting rule, one eye closed, and answers without looking up.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium close shot, c. 1786. A spectacled, clean-shaven surveyor in a dark frock coat bends over a wooden plane-table and sights along a brass alidade, one eye closed and a pencil poised over a pinned paper sheet. He speaks quietly. Grassy inland hillside and hedgerows behind him, soft overcast light. Invented face. No text, no heraldry.

lines.cy: Dim ond tir yr ystad. Dal y polyn yn syth. Mae'r cynllun cynta'n dechrau heddi.
lines.en: Only the estate's land. Hold the pole straight. The first plan starts today.
lines.es: Solo la tierra de la finca. Sostené el jalón derecho. El primer plano empieza hoy.
lines.review: cy: native review (cynta'n, heddi: southern forms)

shots.direction: About 14 s. A top-down still of the plane-table sheet. A pencil traces the first field boundaries as faint lines, without lettering. A slow drift across the paper. Ambience: pencil scratch, wind. Captions only.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 top-down close-up, c. 1786. A sheet of laid paper is pinned to a wooden plane-table, with faint graphite lines sketching irregular field boundaries and hedge lines and no writing or letters. A brass sighting rule and a hand holding a pencil in a dark wool cuff rest on it, with a small brass compass at the corner. Soft overcast light. No text, no heraldry, no seals or devices.

captions.text: 1547: a family research note records a 1,000-year lease of 'Cydwin' from Sir George Herbert to Vaughan. The lease itself is not yet found (EV-0002).
1552–1824: a family research note gives the holding as 'Cedfin / Cydfin / Ken fin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm' in Bute estate records. The documents are not yet produced (EV-0003).

shots.direction: About 14 s. A wide closing still. Dai walks the chain forward to the next hedge while the surveyor stays at the table. Beyond them, a farmhouse roof and yard sit among the fields on the hill. A slow pull-back. Captions only.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 wide shot, inland Llandough hillside c. 1786. A big man in a waistcoat drags a surveyor's chain across a hedged field toward the next hedge-bank. A spectacled man in a dark frock coat stands at a plane-table in the foreground. Further up the hill stand a stone farmhouse with a slate roof and a farmyard among small fields, with oak woods and a distant river marsh below. Overcast late-morning light. No text, no heraldry, no coast.

captions.text: 1667: Williams family occupancy begins, as Mary Buckler later recounted. An earlier written source is awaited (CH-0003).
Looking ahead to 1824: David Stewart's survey of the Bute estates, plan 19, names the holding 'Cedfin or Tŷ Mawr', the oldest record found so far that names the house (EV-0211).

continuity: The chain moves on toward the farmhouse on the hill. In the next scene a surveyor sets up his board in its yard and draws the plan of Tŷ Mawr, then 'Gedrych property'.
